name: libarchive-abaa707d-blind28
instr:
# Multi-format archive toolkit: diagnosing broken behaviour without a test suite

I use this toolkit both as a library and through its command line program for ordinary packing and unpacking work, and a great deal of that work now comes out wrong. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the formats involved changed and nothing about the way I call it changed: the same jobs that used to come out right now come out wrong, and in several places something that used to be accepted is refused outright.

Taking apart containers that other tools produced. An entry held sparsely in the classic Unix streaming format of GNU vintage, whose holes are described by per-entry extended key/value records, unpacks into a file whose data and gaps sit in the wrong places, and when that description claims more room than the entry itself occupies the whole thing goes through in silence where I expected a warning. A member of a 7-Zip container whose stream was prepared with the filter meant for PowerPC executables comes back as bytes that are not the file that went in, so the member either refuses to come out or comes out as rubbish. Content pulled from a CAB file is truncated or shifted against the original once I am a little way into the compressed stream. An LHA/LZH file fails outright or hands back the wrong bytes for its members, tiny ones included.
